task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-05-23, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
If PNR fail then PULL_UP is a real league-wide counter, it should show lift>0 in >=70% of units with median lift>2pp.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

research_concepts: PNR fail as a defensive outcome label
PULL_UP shot as a candidate counter
league-wide unit lift relative to a baseline
derived play-type possession records from play-by-play
methodological_questions: How is 'PNR fail' operationally defined from play-by-play or derived possession records without using the outcome being tested?
What is a 'unit' (team-season, team-game, matchup, or possession type), and what is the baseline against which lift is measured?
Does the claimed threshold (lift>0 in >=70% of units and median lift>2pp) need a pre-specified baseline, direction, and test statistic?
Can lift after PNR fail be separated from shot quality, personnel, and defensive scheme?
evidence_establishes: retrieve_history returned zero records (n_results = 0), so no earlier study by this project on PNR fail, PULL_UP counters, or unit-lift thresholds is available in this setting.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether PULL_UP is a counter to PNR fail, league-wide or otherwise.
Whether the 70% and 2pp thresholds are reasonable or previously tested.
Whether any earlier approach to this question failed, and why.
own_inferences: The question as posed is underspecified: 'PNR fail', 'PULL_UP', 'unit', and 'baseline' are not defined, so the threshold cannot be evaluated as written.

Using the 2025-26 playoffs before 2026-06-21 would include partial data relative to the question date of 2026-05-23, so only complete regular-season data (2022-23 to 2025-26, with 2025-26 complete from 2026-04-13) is clean for this date.
A test is feasible at team-season granularity (about 30 teams over 4 seasons, roughly 120 units), but power for a 2pp effect against game-to-game and shot-quality noise is probably limited.
Any positive lift from PULL_UP after PNR fail is observational and could reflect opponent shot selection or lineup context, not a counter that defenders can execute.
uncertainties: Exact definition of PNR fail (turnover, no shot, low-quality shot, or a derived label that uses points) and whether it is measured on the same possessions used for the outcome.
Whether the PULL_UP label in the derived possession records is reliable and consistent across seasons.
Whether the 70% and 2pp criteria are applied to units with equal weight and what the baseline (league average, team average, or possession-type average) is.
Rule changes and style drift across 2022-23 to 2025-26 that could shift PULL_UP frequency and efficiency.
No prior work was retrieved, so the already_answered status is unknown.

historical_effect.explanation: No records were returned, so the decision rests on the task statement and data description alone. The absence of prior work means no earlier finding or failed approach could change the plan, and the decision reflects the question's underspecification rather than any historical result.

blocking_constraints.text: If PNR fail is defined using the same points or possession outcomes later used to measure PULL_UP lift, the test is circular. The definition must be fixed on data that does not include the outcome.
Around 120 team-season units give limited power to detect a 2pp median lift with the 70% positive-lift criterion, especially after splitting by PNR-fail context.

PULL_UP frequency and efficiency after PNR fail depend on shot quality, ball-handler quality, screener, and defensive matchup. Observational lift is not attributable to the counter without adjustment.

prior_work.summary: No earlier study was retrieved (retrieve_history returned n_results = 0). Whether this question has been answered elsewhere, or by this project, is unknown and cannot be assessed from the available records.

risks.text: PNR fail may be defined from possession outcomes (turnover, points) that also define the lift outcome, producing circular or inflated effects.
Unit count (about 30 teams over 4 seasons) is small for detecting a 2pp median lift, and the 70% criterion amplifies noise.
Shot quality, distance, shooter skill, lineup, and opponent defensive scheme all co-vary with PULL_UP use after PNR fail; no adjustment is specified.
If units are chosen because they had high PNR fail or high PULL_UP rates in a given season, regression to the mean will inflate apparent lift.
Play-type and sub-type tagging in play-by-play and derived records may misclassify PULL_UP, PNR, and fail outcomes, attenuating or biasing lift.
Many play types and counter candidates could be screened; the reported result could reflect the best of several comparisons.
Pace, three-point rate, and defensive scheme changed across 2022-23 to 2025-26, so pooling seasons may mix different regimes.
PULL_UP after PNR fail may be rare in some units, making lift estimates unstable.

design.estimand: Within-unit difference in points per possession (pp, shot-based efficiency) on possessions after a PNR fail that end with a PULL_UP attempt, versus matched possessions after PNR fail that do not, averaged across units. Interpreted as an association, not a causal counter effect, unless the adjusted design supports otherwise.
design.unit: Team-season (primary). Team-season-matchup is a secondary, sensitivity unit. The unit must be fixed before analysis.
design.sample: Regular-season play-by-play and derived possession records for 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and 2025-26 (2025-26 regular season only from 2026-04-13 onward, which is complete). Exclude 2025-26 playoffs for the 2026-05-23 analysis date because they are partial. Playoff data can be a separate pre-specified sensitivity analysis after 2026-06-21.
design.power: Before analysis, run a simulation with the observed PNR-fail and PULL_UP frequencies per team-season to estimate power for a 2pp median lift and the 70% positive-lift criterion. Proceed only if power to detect 2pp is at least 0.8 at the chosen alpha; otherwise report the criterion as underpowered and do not claim a conclusion.
design.controls: Adjust for shot distance and shot type, shooter identity or shooting-talent proxy, ball-handler and screener identity, defensive matchup minutes, lineup, game score margin, and period/clock. Use a matched or regression design. Define the PNR-fail label from possession data that excludes the PULL_UP outcome, using a rule set before analysis.
design.falsification: Pre-specify a placebo counter (a play type with no hypothesized relationship to PNR fail, e.g., post-up or transition) and a placebo outcome (a non-shot outcome). The claim is falsified if the placebo shows comparable lift, or if adjusted lift is not positive in at least 70% of units with median above 2pp.
design.multiplicity: Pre-register the primary criterion (PULL_UP only, team-season units, one baseline). Correct any secondary comparisons across play types for multiple testing (for example Holm or FDR), and report all counters screened.
design.decision_rule: Claim support only if: (a) PNR-fail and PULL_UP labels are fixed without outcome leakage; (b) power is adequate for the stated 2pp threshold; (c) the adjusted lift is positive in at least 70% of units with median lift above 2pp; (d) the placebo counter does not show the same lift; (e) the result holds in the leave-one-season-out check. Otherwise report inconclusive or rejected, and do not describe PULL_UP as a league-wide counter.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2025-26 regular seasons (2025-26 complete from 2026-04-13), play-by-play, substitution intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes, box scores, and the derived possession graph as of 2026-05-23. Record the data snapshot date and [source] build version before running any analysis.
